The first peeked header does not match either accepted `b_info` shape for this gap, so execution enters the `bad b_info` recovery path. The Stage 01 run printed `[WARNING] bad b_info at 0x623f8`, confirming this branch on the saved witness.

Recovery rewinds 32 bytes before `pos` and copies a 64-byte witness-controlled window into stack local `peek_arr`. Using the observed warning location `0x623f8`, this buffer spans file offsets `0x623d8..0x62417` in the staged PoC.

The recovery scan searches the 64-byte stack buffer for the little-endian encoding of `size`. In the staged witness, bytes `60 36 00 00` appear at relative offsets `57..60` of this window, so `find_le32` can return `boff = 57`; that exact offset is also consistent with ASan's later 4-byte read starting at `peek_arr + 61`.

Root-cause step. This guard rejects only a missing match. Because `boff == 57` is nonnegative, control falls through even though `57 + sizeof(b_info) == 69` exceeds the 64-byte `peek_arr` extent by 5 bytes.

The unchecked tail offset is reinterpreted as a full `b_info *`. With `boff = 57`, `bp` names a 12-byte struct that starts 7 bytes before the end of `peek_arr`, so later field loads run off the stack buffer.

Sink. `b_info::sz_cpr` is 4 bytes after the aliased struct base, so this load starts at `peek_arr + 61`. `get_le32` calls `get_ne32`, which copies 4 bytes from that address and overruns the 64-byte stack array by one byte.
